🚀 SketchForge-3D | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Quickly designing and exporting 3D models for various purposes, such as 3D printing or prototyping, directly within a web browser without complex setup.
✨ Key Features: • Local-first projects stored in browser storage • Real 3D workplane with camera and snap controls • Primitive shape library (boxes, cylinders, spheres, etc.) • Solid and hole workflow for boolean operations • Boolean Intersection
📖 Summary: SketchForge-3D is a local-first, browser-based 3D design editor that allows users to build, modify, import, and export 3D models directly in their web browser. It focuses on a streamlined workflow for creating parts without requiring accounts or heavy software installations.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 pgrok | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Exposing local development servers or applications to the internet for testing, collaboration, or public access, with the added benefit of secure HTTPS connections and real-time monitoring.
✨ Key Features: • Expose local ports to the internet • Automatic HTTPS via Caddy • SSH reverse tunnels • Interactive TUI dashboard • HTTP request inspection
📖 Summary: pgrok is a personal alternative to ngrok that exposes local ports to the internet using SSH tunnels and Caddy for automatic HTTPS. It features an interactive TUI dashboard for monitoring and debugging.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ ProxyBridge | C
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide transparent system-wide proxying for TCP and UDP traffic on Windows, macOS, and Linux, allowing users to route traffic through SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies on a per-application basis.
✨ Key Features: • Universal proxy client for Windows, macOS, and Linux • Transparent proxy routing for TCP and UDP traffic • Supports SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies
📖 Summary: ProxyBridge is a universal proxy client for Windows, macOS, and Linux that acts as a Proxifier alternative. It enables transparent redirection of TCP and UDP traffic from applications through SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies, allowing granular control over traffic routing, blocking, or allowing on a per-application basis.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 textual-web | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To make Textual-based terminal applications and raw terminals accessible and shareable through a web browser interface.
✨ Key Features: • Publish Textual apps and terminals on the web • Run TUIs in a browser • Generate public URLs for apps and terminals • Serve multiple apps and terminals via configuration • Support for serving raw terminals with optional commands
📖 Summary: Textual Web allows users to run Textual applications and terminals directly in their web browser. It acts as a bridge, making TUIs accessible remotely and shareable via public URLs, simplifying the deployment and access of terminal-based applications.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ swarms | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Orchestrating complex multi-agent AI systems in production environments.
✨ Key Features: • Enterprise-grade multi-agent orchestration • Production-ready architectures (sequential, concurrent, hierarchical) • Scalable and adaptive systems • Backward compatibility with leading agent frameworks • Interoperability with protocols like MCP, x402, skills
📖 Summary: Swarms is an enterprise-grade, production-ready framework for orchestrating multi-agent systems. It provides scalable and adaptive architectures for sequential, concurrent, and hierarchical agent interactions, with backward compatibility and interoperability with various AI protocols.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 imgcompress | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a private, self-hosted solution for batch image processing, including compression, format conversion, and AI background removal, for users who want to maintain full control over their data and avoid cloud-based services.
✨ Key Features: • Support for over 70 image formats (including PSD, HEIC, RAW, EPS, TIFF, WebP)
📖 Summary: ImgCompress is a self-hosted, Docker-based image processing toolbox that offers a comprehensive suite of tools for compression, format conversion, and AI-powered background removal. It operates entirely locally, ensuring user privacy and data security by processing all files within the user's own container without external uploads.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
